'''Hong Wang''' ({{lang-zh|s=王虹|p=Wáng Hóng}}; born 1991) is a Chinese mathematician known for her research in [[Fourier analysis]] and [[geometric measure theory]]. She was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] in 2026 for her contributions to [[Fourier restriction conjecture|Fourier restriction]], [[Falconer's conjecture]], Furstenberg sets in the plane, and the [[Kakeya conjecture]]. She is the third woman and the first Chinese woman to win the award.<ref name=":2" /> 

==Early life and education==
Wang was born in [[Guilin]], [[Guangxi]], China, in 1991.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2026-07-24 |title=Fields Medal: Chinese win world's top Maths prize for first time |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvg84gp8xx4o |access-date=2026-07-26 |website=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> Her parents were both schoolteachers at a local middle school, with her father being a mathematics teacher.<ref name="quantamagazine26">{{cite magazine |last=Wolchover |first=Natalie |author-link=Natalie Wolchover |title=Hong Wang Wins 2026 Fields Medal, the Third Woman Ever |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/hong-wang-wins-2026-fields-medal-the-third-woman-ever-20260723/ |magazine=Quanta Magazine |language=en |date=23 July 2026 |access-date=24 July 2026 |archive-date=23 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723205944/https://www.quantamagazine.org/hong-wang-wins-2026-fields-medal-the-third-woman-ever-20260723/ |url-status=live }}</ref> At age 6, she developed an interest in [[incidence geometry]].<ref name="quantamagazine26" /> While in primary school, she [[Grade skipping|skipped]] two grades.<ref name=":0" /> In 2004, Wang began attending {{ill|桂林市桂林中學|lt=Guilin High School|zh}}. She was placed outside of the top 100 students in her first year of high school, but, by her final year, was ranked in the top ten of her class.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Han |first=Yangmei |date=July 24, 2026 |title=From a "Hidden Figure" in Peking University's Mathematics Department to a Fields Medal Winner |url=https://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2026/7/[path] |access-date=2026-08-07 |website=[[ScienceNet]] |language=zh}}</ref> 

In 2007, at age 16, Wang took the [[Gaokao]] and won early admission to [[Peking University]]. At the time, the university reserved a single space for a [[mathematical sciences]] applicant from Guangxi, and Wang, whose score in the entrance exam was below the cutoff, was redirected to study [[earth science]] instead of mathematics.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pouille |first=Jordan |date=2026-08-06 |title=Hong Wang's Fields Medal win reignites debate across China over how its top researchers emerge |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/08/06/hong-wang-s-fields-medal-win-reignites-debate-across-china-over-how-its-top-researchers-emerge_6756199_4.html |access-date=2026-08-07 |work=[[Le Monde]] |language= |issn=1950-6244}}</ref> But in her sophomore year, after sitting the university's transfer exam, she switched her academic major to mathematics, focusing on [[algebraic analysis]] and [[mathematical analysis]].<ref name=":1" />

Wang graduated from [[Peking University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in mathematics in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Hongce |date=26 May 2025 |title=Mathematician Wang Hong appointed as a tenured professor at the Institute of Advanced Studies in Law |url=https://www.stdaily.com/web/gjxw/2025-05/26/content_344386.html |access-date=18 July 2026 |website=[[Science and Technology Daily]] |language=zh}}</ref> Her classmates included [[Yunqing Tang]] and [[Yu Deng]].<ref name=":32">{{Cite web|date=23 July 2026|title=Wang Hong and Deng Yu become first Chinese nationals to win Fields Medal|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3361633/fields-medal-win-wang-hong-deng-yu-are-first-chinese-nationals-score-top-maths-honour|access-date=23 July 2026|website=South China Morning Post|language=en|archive-date=23 July 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723182605/https://www.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3361633/fields-medal-win-wang-hong-deng-yu-are-first-chinese-nationals-score-top-maths-honour|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=滚动播报|date=7 November 2025|script-title=zh:她成为首位摘获数论最高奖的华人女数学家，毕业于上海中学，是王虹本科同学|url=https://finance.sina.com.cn/jjxw/2025-11-07/doc-infwqrfw6028555.shtml|access-date=18 July 2026|website=finance.sina.com.cn}}</ref> She then pursued postgraduate studies in France and earned two graduate credentials in 2014: a ''[[Diplôme d'Ingénieur]]'' ({{Literal translation|engineer's degree}})<ref name="one">{{cite web |title=MIT mathematicians awarded 2022 New Frontiers Prize |url=https://news.mit.edu/2021/mit-mathematicians-awarded-2022-new-frontiers-prize-0909 |website=[[MIT News]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909173602/https://news.mit.edu/2021/mit-mathematicians-awarded-2022-new-frontiers-prize-0909 |archive-date=9 September 2021 |date=9 September 2021}}</ref> from [[École polytechnique]] and a [[Master of Science]] degree from [[Paris-Sud University]].<ref>{{cite web |script-title=zh:跟随自己的兴趣和感觉 专访王虹校友 |url=https://www.sohu.com/a/732882837_121123993 |website=sohu.com |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250305041359/https://www.sohu.com/a/732882837_121123993 |archive-date=5 March 2025 |date=1 November 2023|trans-title=Follow your own interests and feelings. Interview with alumnus Wang Hong}}</ref> In 2019, she earned her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] degree in mathematics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT). Her doctoral advisor was [[Larry Guth]].<ref name="one" />

== Career ==

After completing her doctorate in 2019, Wang was a postdoctoral member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], from 2019 to 2021. She served as an assistant professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] from 2021 to 2023.<ref name="quantamagazine26" />

Wang moved to the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] (NYU) as an associate professor in 2023.<ref name="quantamagazine26" /> In September 2025, she became a full professor at NYU, while also being appointed as a permanent professor of mathematics at the [[Institut des hautes études scientifiques]] (IHES) in France.<ref name="IHESappointment">{{cite web |title=Hong Wang joins IHES as Permanent Professor of Mathematics |url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/hong-wang-ihes/ |website=Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques |date=27 May 2025 |access-date=24 July 2026 |archive-date=27 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250527075938/https://www.ihes.fr/en/hong-wang-ihes/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="IHESFields2026">{{cite web |title=Hong Wang, Permanent Professor at IHES, awarded the 2026 Fields Medal |url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/hong-wang2026-fields-medal/ |website=Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques |date=23 July 2026 |access-date=24 July 2026 |archive-date=24 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260724103356/https://www.ihes.fr/en/hong-wang2026-fields-medal/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In April 2026, NYU named Wang a [[Silver Professor]] of Mathematics, the most prestigious named professorship NYU can offer its faculty.<ref name="NYUSilver">{{cite web |title=Hong Wang, Russel Caflisch, Sanjeev Khanna Receive Silver Professorships |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1505/ |website=Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences |publisher=New York University |date=2 April 2026 |access-date=24 July 2026 |archive-date=21 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260521075845/https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1505/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Academic research ==

Wang's research is in [[harmonic analysis]] and [[geometric measure theory]], particularly the family of [[Kakeya set|Kakeya-type problems]] connecting Fourier analysis with incidence geometry, [[partial differential equation]]s, combinatorics and number theory.<ref name="quantamagazine26"/> As a doctoral student, she developed new approaches to the [[restriction conjecture|Fourier restriction problem]] using incidence geometry and contributed to work on the Falconer distance problem. In 2019, Wang, [[Larry Guth]], and [[Ruixiang Zhang]] proved the two-dimensional case of the local smoothing conjecture. In 2023, Wang and Kevin Ren proved the two-dimensional Furstenberg set conjecture.<ref name="quantamagazine26"/>

One of Wang's best-known research projects was conducted with Joshua Zahl on the three-dimensional [[Kakeya conjecture]]. In 2022, they proved the conjecture for a class known as ''sticky Kakeya sets'', eliminating a major family of possible counterexamples.<ref name="Cepelewicz2023">{{cite magazine |last=Cepelewicz |first=Jordana |title=New Proof Threads the Needle on a Sticky Geometry Problem |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/new-proof-threads-the-needle-on-a-sticky-geometry-problem-20230711/ |magazine=Quanta Magazine |date=11 July 2023 |access-date=24 July 2026 |archive-date=24 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260724103321/https://www.quantamagazine.org/new-proof-threads-the-needle-on-a-sticky-geometry-problem-20230711/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2025, they posted a 127-page proof of the full conjecture in three dimensions, establishing that every Kakeya set in <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math> has both [[Hausdorff dimension|Hausdorff]] and [[Minkowski–Bouligand dimension|Minkowski dimension]] three.<ref name="Howlett2025">{{cite magazine |last=Howlett |first=Joseph |title='Once in a Century' Proof Settles Math's Kakeya Conjecture |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/once-in-a-century-proof-settles-maths-kakeya-conjecture-20250314/ |magazine=Quanta Magazine |date=14 March 2025 |access-date=24 July 2026 |archive-date=24 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260724034033/https://www.quantamagazine.org/once-in-a-century-proof-settles-maths-kakeya-conjecture-20250314/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The proof combined the earlier sticky-set analysis with a multiscale study of "grainy" configurations of thin tubes, iteratively improving known lower bounds until the full dimension was obtained.<ref name="Howlett2025"/><ref name="quantamagazine26"/> The result is considered foundational because Kakeya estimates are closely connected to major problems in harmonic analysis, including the Fourier restriction and local smoothing conjectures.<ref name="Howlett2025"/>

==Awards==
[[File:Hong Wang (王虹) - Q103368586.jpg|thumb|Wang in 2024]]
Wang was a 2022 recipient of the [[Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize]], given "for advances on the [[restriction conjecture]], the local smoothing conjecture, and related problems".<ref name ='one'/><ref name="two">{{cite web |title=Mathematician Hong Wang wins New Frontiers Prize |url=https://newsroom.ucla.edu/dept/faculty/mathematician-hong-wang-wins-new-frontiers-prize |website=[[University of California, Los Angeles]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909183654/https://newsroom.ucla.edu/dept/faculty/mathematician-hong-wang-wins-new-frontiers-prize |archive-date=9 September 2021 |date=9 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Laureates |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3912 |website=[[Breakthrough Prize]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909173001/https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3912 |archive-date=9 September 2021}}</ref>

Wang was a 2025 recipient of the [[Salem Prize]], given "for her role in solutions to major open problems in harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory".<ref name="Salem2025">{{cite web | title=2025 Salem Prize Winners | website=Institute for Advanced Study | date=27 October 2025 | url=https://www.ias.edu/math/2025-salem-prize-winners | access-date=29 October 2025 | archive-date=5 November 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251105123426/https://www.ias.edu/math/2025-salem-prize-winners | url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="cims1487">{{cite web |title=Hong Wang Awarded Ostrowski Prize, Salem Prize, and ICCM Gold Medal of Mathematics |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1487/ |publisher=[[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] |date=24 November 2025 |access-date=30 June 2026 |archive-date=20 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260420001236/https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1487/ |url-status=live }}</ref> She was awarded the 2025 [[International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians|ICCM]] Gold Medal of Mathematics from the International Consortium of Chinese Mathematicians, given to "outstanding mathematicians of Chinese descent under the age of 45 for their achievements in the research of pure and applied mathematics, and for their great contributions to the development of mathematics".<ref name="cims1487" /> She was also a 2025 recipient of the [[Ostrowski Prize]], given for her "influential work in harmonic analysis, solving central problems in the field like the Kakeya set conjecture in three dimensions or the restriction conjecture in higher dimensions".<ref>{{cite web |title=The prize and the prize winners |url=https://www.ostrowski.ch/index_e.php?ifile=preis |publisher=Ostrowski Foundation |access-date=20 November 2025 |archive-date=11 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250911161109/https://www.ostrowski.ch/index_e.php?ifile=preis |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Citation for Hong Wang |url=https://www.ostrowski.ch/pdf/preis2025.pdf |publisher=Ostrowski Foundation |access-date=20 November 2025}}</ref>

In 2026, she was awarded the [[Sadosky Prize]] from the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], given "for solving central problems in harmonic analysis through the introduction of ground-breaking ideas. In particular, for substantial contributions to the Fourier restriction problem, the Kakeya conjecture, and geometric measure theory".<ref>{{cite web |title=AWM Sadosky Research Prize in Analysis 2026 |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-sadosky-research-prize/awm-sadosky-research-prize-2026/ |publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]] |access-date=30 October 2025 |archive-date=20 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251120013604/https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-sadosky-research-prize/awm-sadosky-research-prize-2026/ |url-status=live }}</ref> She also received the [[Clay Research Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.claymath.org/people/hong-wang/ |title=Clay Research Award 2026 |access-date=15 April 2026 |archive-date=19 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260419061651/https://www.claymath.org/people/hong-wang/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

On 23 July 2026, Hong Wang was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] by the [[International Mathematical Union]], alongside [[Yu Deng]], [[John Pardon]], and [[Jacob Tsimerman]], for her contributions to harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory, including the proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture.<ref>{{cite web | title=Fields Medals 2026 | website=www.mathunion.org | url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-2026 | access-date=23 July 2026 | archive-date=23 July 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723135714/https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-2026 | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Castelvecchi |first=Davide |date=2026-07-23 |title=Rising stars of mathematics awarded prestigious 2026 Fields Medal |journal=Nature |language=en |doi=10.1038/d41586-026-02169-1 |pmid=42493565 |issn=1476-4687}}</ref> She was the first Chinese woman to win the Fields Medal.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.wxxinews.org/npr-news/2026-07-23/in-a-first-chinese-woman-wins-the-prestigious-fields-medal|title=In a first, Chinese woman wins the prestigious Fields Medal|date=23 July 2026}}</ref>
